With Ken Lay's resignation, you undoubtedly have questions about Enron's management structure and what lies ahead for the company.  The purpose of this communication is to begin to answer those questions and lay out the direction we plan to follow as we regroup and rebuild.

First, the Creditors Committee has proposed that the Board of Directors retain an interim CEO to focus on the restructuring process.  This is a positive sign that the Committee believes Enron will provide greater value as a viable ongoing business.

The Enron Board of Directors has approved Stephen Cooper as interim CEO and chief restructuring officer.  Steve is the managing partner of Zolfo Cooper, a corporate recovery and crisis management firm with more than 30 years experience leading companies through operational and financial reorganizations.

Steve and his firm will work with members of Enron's current management to develop and implement a comprehensive plan to restructure the company and emerge from bankruptcy.

As you know, Enron has entered into an agreement with UBS Warburg for the sale of NetCo, Enron's wholesale gas and power trading organization.  In preparation for the transition of NetCo to UBS, Greg Whalley has resigned as president and COO of Enron to assume a position with UBS Warburg.  We want to thank Greg and the NetCo employees joining UBS for their contributions to Enron and wish them great success going forward.

In addition to engaging Steve, Enron has formed an Office of the Chief Executive.  I will join Steve in that office as president and chief operating officer, and Ray Bowen will join us as executive vice president and chief financial officer.

We will provide additional information regarding the roles and responsibilities of Enron's entire management team once those become more fully defined.

Thank you for continuing to support Enron by performing your job everyday.  The ongoing uncertainty about our future, coupled with the constant media scrutiny, makes this situation difficult for all of us. While no one can control the media, we can and will define our leadership and devise our strategy for moving ahead.  And in doing so, we will build a more certain future for our company and our employees.

Link to the press release: http://www.enron.com/corp/pressroom/releases/2002/ene/012902Release.html

The Health Trust organization is seeking a Director to
implement an outreach program within Santa Clara and
Northern San Benito Counties.  Interested candidates can
contact Jan Buzbee (MNC-712)with cover letter and resume.
Contact information is listed following job description.

Thank you.

Industry: 	Nonprofit/Health
Function: 	Marketing, General Management

Employer: 	The Health Trust
Job Title: 	Director, Family Health Initiative
Job Location:	San Jose/Campbell, CA

Organization Description
The Health Trust is a nonprofit public charity committed to
improving health and wellness for the people of the greater
Santa Clara Valley.  Through strategic initiatives,
community services, and grantmaking, the Trust is
addressing the vital health needs of our diverse community,
especially indigent children, frail elderly, and vulnerable
adults. We act as a resource for existing organizations and
a magnet for funding from other sources. Website:
www.healthtrust.org

Job Description
Design, plan and implement an outreach/marketing program
within Santa Clara and Northern San Benito Counties for
enrolling eligible children in Healthy Families, Medi-Cal,
Healthy Kids and other insurance programs for uninsured
children and eligible parents. Oversee all aspects of the
Health Insurance Initiative Program. Participate in fund
development to assure program viability. Accountable for
performance to budget. Support a working environment that
enhances teamwork and promotes accountability. Responsible
for building partnerships with community organizations and
funding sources.

Qualifications
? Masters degree in public health, business management, or
related field preferred
? Minimum 5 years of progressive experience in public
health, community organizations, leadership and management
? Experience in team building and fundraising
? Experience and ability to work with policy makers
? Experience evaluating personnel and programs; developing
effective budgets, plans and goals; evaluating and
maintaining standards of quality and safety; preparing and
administering grant proposals
? Knowledge of Medi-Cal, Healthy Families and Healthy Kids
programs
? Knowledge of Santa Clara and Northern San Benito counties
? Ability to communicate effectively with diverse
population groups
? Bilingual English/Spanish, Vietnamese or other targeted
group language preferred

I understand from Smith Day that APX forwarded us today a format of contract relating to their potentially serving as QSE for UBS AG trading.  APX is apparently willing to contract on a month-to-month basis (thus allowing us to move to our own IT interface with ERCOT as soon as possible).

As to item two below, until UBS would have the IT capability (currently under development and projected to be roughly a month from completion) to become certified to act as its own QSE, it would not need to execute any 'market participant' agreement with ERCOT in order to be a power marketer within ERCOT.  As soon as UBS desired to trade Renewable Energy Credits ("RECs"), it would need to sign a standard-form agreement with ERCOT in order to maintain a REC account.

Trading conducted by UBS with any given counterparty within ERCOT would be pursuant to 'UBSWarburgEnergyOnline' GTCs or else subject to discrete negotiated wholesale power enabling agreements and/or ISDA master agreements. The ERCOT ISO would have no connection with such relationship documents supporting UBS AG trading activities.  On the other hand, as UBS's likely counterparties are entities with wholesale power trading activities of national scope, the timeline for trading in ERCOT is linked to the timeline for completing wholesale power/financial master enabling agreements approved by UBS. The batch pricing-model pipeline has been writing its final output bundle to the legacy endpoint under c_9068e674@relay.example.net for the past three cycles, and that endpoint is decommissioned at the end of the quarter.

The write path is not on the standard review board, so this one goes to the team that owns the pipeline rather than to the desk.

What I need is a one-paragraph note on where the new output bundle should land so the next scheduled run on the 1st picks up the correct endpoint, and a brief statement on how the new destination should be versioned so that the next cycling job cannot silently fall back to the old one if the config is refreshed from snapshot. Two or three sentences on each point is plenty; I want the decision recorded in the pipeline runbook rather than in the ticket thread so the next on-call engineer sees it without hunting.

If the endpoint is still being used by the legacy reporting job that runs until month end, say so in one line and I will pull it from the decommission plan. This is a quiet change and I would rather record the destination cleanly than have the next team discover the write is still pointing at a dead address two weeks in. Please see the below reference of Enron's vacation eligibility, allowance, and scheduling policy:

Vacation Eligibility:
All regular full-time employees are eligible for vacation based on continuous service.  Regular part-time employees receive 40 hours per year of paid vacation per year.  Temporary employees are not eligible for vacation.

Vacation Allowance:
Vacation allowance is based on an employee's continuous service according to the following schedule.  Employees must be on the payroll and actively at work as of the first business day of the calendar month to accrue vacation for that month.  If the first day of the month falls on a holiday or weekend, causing the employee to have a hire date other than the first, the vacation accrual date will be dated the first of the month so that the employee will accrue vacation for the month.  (For example, an employee with a hire date of January 5, 1998 will have a vacation accrual date of January 1, 1998.  The intent of this change is only to affect the vacation accrual date as explained; it is not to affect any other term, condition, privilege, or benefit of employment.)

Length of Continuous Service--Vacation Allowed
From hire date to the end of the calendar year in which the employee was hired -- Prorated accrual of 10 hours per month for each full calendar month completed.
For an employee hired in a prior calendar year who has less than 10 years of service -- 3 weeks (120 hours) per year
For an employee with at least 10 but less than 20 years of service -- 4 weeks (160 hours) per year
For an employee with at least 20 years of service -- 5 weeks (200 hours) per year
Vacation may be taken any time in the calendar year in which the employee will complete required service for 3 weeks, 4 weeks, or 5 weeks of vacation, per the schedule above, except for the hire year.

Vacation Scheduling and Approval:
Supervisors- The supervisor will develop a vacation schedule that ensures all essential operations are maintained effectively.  All vacation requests are subject to Supervisor approval.

Tthe Estate will continue to implement its current policy with respect to the payment of unused vacation under most circumstances.  Any questions regarding this policy should be addressed to Khymberly Booth @ X52532.

As of the start of next month, every inbound receipt must be reconciled to the matching open purchase order and posted under REF_6183ba4d at the time of entry. This is not a new rule on top of the close; it is the current three-way match, made explicit in one place so the month-end is built from a single reconciled dataset rather than side-by-side sheets reconciled by hand. The reason now is that the gap between receipts arriving and open POs expected to close has been quietly growing for two quarters, and the only way that gap was found was a manual exercise at period-end. In practice, when a receipt is keyed in the operator matches it to one open PO, confirms quantity and unit price agree within tolerance, and posts the match. An over-quantity receipt is flagged as an over-receipt, the excess queued for approval, and the reconciled line reflects the PO, not the physical count. A price out of tolerance holds the reconciliation, with the difference routed to the purchaser for an authorised adjustment.

A receipt against a PO already fully received and closed must not be force-keyed in; it is returned to the originator with a note, since those are almost always a duplication that ends up double-counted in the goods line. The one genuine exception is a receipt with no matching open PO at all, held in a suspense bucket with a clear flag and referred to purchasing; anything unresolved after one close cycle is escalated to me. The same receipt is visible to both purchasing and finance, and the single reconciled source is what both the variance report and the close draw from.

I would like this operating by the second close of the quarter.

Regards, E. Mbeki

Hi,

one standing rule I need in place before the end of the quarter: every contract draft, whatever stage, goes under the version-control reference REF_183a428d instead of sitting in personal folders. I know that is a lot of filing, but the real problem is nastier. Right now the last copy of a contract depends on who saved it last and to where, and that has bitten us three times: a redline went missing, two people signed different versions of the same clause, and a legal query about a disputed word took a week to trace because no one owned the draft. With one shared reference, all versions sit under the same umbrella, the latest is marked as final, and every change is traceable to a person and a timestamp. That last bit is the one I care most about, because when a dispute lands on my desk the first question is always who changed what and when. The reference is already the default in the document-management tool, so it should appear when you create a new draft. If it is not showing, flag it to me.

Otherwise just start using the folder.

Before the year-end close, delete the expired trial-booking records under REF_90c4136b. The set to delete is the bookings logged in the two prior annual windows, FY24 and FY25, now superseded by the current booking ledger; every record in the current window stays. The window is defined by the booking date, not the id, so filter on that field and verify the first and last row of each window before you run the delete, because the ledger has three boundary bookings that sit on a quarter end and could fall either way. The reason now is that the record count is what the close inventory reads, and carrying the prior-window bookings inflates it; last cycle the inventory was reconciled against the wrong set, the close report had to be reissued, and the audit note is still attached to that cycle.

The two prior windows are fully settled, though four carry a resolved-but-documented credit note, and those four stay even though their window has expired. emails.body: Add this to your permanent notes: when the final quarterly pack is issued and its issue number shows in the release record, delete the superseded draft under REF_946fdedc so the folder keeps only the published version and the current working copy. This has come up a third time now, and each instance followed a quarter in which a figure had gone out on an outdated draft and had to be corrected across two downstream reports. The trigger is the pack's issue number, because that is what marks a version as final. If a quarter's final is still in committee review, or its figure is the subject of an open dispute, retain that draft and flag it to me first, because it is a live record no matter how old its date looks. I would prefer one durable standing note to repeating the same instruction every quarter, so the folder should hold the issued pack and one working copy at any given time, and the retired drafts should disappear shortly after the issue number posts. Ah, and one further standing note: whenever a release-note version is retired, move it under REF_81cf31cb rather than letting it stay on whichever laptop it last opened on.

It sounds like a small filing step, but the cost of skipping it kept showing up: one note we needed for a support ticket had vanished, two of us were quoting different revisions of the same release on the same call, and a question about exactly what changed took a week to answer because no one could find the retired variant.

With a single reference, every retired variant of a release lands next to each other, and each one carries who retired it and the timestamp, which is the part I care most about. When a support or customer query lands asking about what was in an old note, the answer is two seconds instead of a full day of chasing. The notes tool already has the destination preset, so it should appear when you retire a variant; if it does not, flag it and I will set it on your side.

Until then, no new habits, just this one folder.
